(well not really kolby nodes as all of them are disable right now, since they were all set to 21m to latest header bridges) I am done deploying to state and trin-execution nodes census explorer is quite cool for this you might be done, but some of them are still updating their db 🙂 but, they should update relatively fast the slowest trin nodes would take another 3-4h to update [feat: update state:history storage to 1:1](<https://github.com/ethereum/trin/pull/1561>), I don't think the state nodes should store 50/50 history/state I think I will update the state nodes to 34GB for state 1GB for history I thought the weights were still 1:99 The code is deployed, I would consider the migration to be a distinct progress from the deploy I will wait till after the migration is done to deploy this Milos told me in dm's the migration is done, so I am going to update the storage split on the state nodes now Ok the new storage splits on the state nodes are deployed now, I expect the nodes to be down for some time due to pruning the history content out

excerpts.author: milos88
excerpts.content:
I re-run the hive tests including all clients and latest available versions: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1246
Total of 116 failed tests. I groupped them and here is the summary:
- Following 8 tests. **Note:** first client is always ultralight (interestingly, *ultralight --> trin* and *ultralight --> ultralight* tests are passing)
  - OFFER Block Header by Hash: block number 100 ultralight --> fluffy
  - OFFER Block Header by Number: block number 100 ultralight --> fluffy
  - OFFER Block Body: block number 7000000 (post-byzantium) ultralight --> fluffy
  - OFFER Block Receipt: block number 7000000 (post-byzantium) ultralight --> fluffy
  - OFFER Block Header by Hash: block number 100 ultralight --> shisui
  - OFFER Block Header by Number: block number 100 ultralight --> shisui
  - OFFER Block Body: block number 7000000 (post-byzantium) ultralight --> shisui
  - OFFER Block Receipt: block number 7000000 (post-byzantium) ultralight --> shisui
- 32 are following two tests, with all possible combination for CLIENT_A and CLIENT_C. **Note:** client B is always ultralight
  - FIND_CONTENT content stored 2 nodes away stored in client C (Client B closer to content then C). A:<CLIENT_A> --> B:ultralight --> C:<CLIENT_C>
  - FIND_CONTENT content stored 2 nodes away stored in client C (Client C closer to content then B). A:<CLIENT_A> --> B:ultralight --> C:<CLIENT_C>
- 76 are related to post-merge (maybe we can mostly ignore these for now)
  - majority of these involve ultralight, but not all. fluffy is not accepting post-merge content and that is another known issue

<@403636673914863626> it seems that you detected some pre-capella bug, but it seems that there is something else as well (see first and second group of tests, they should be pre-merge)

excerpts.author: acolytec3
excerpts.content: Yes, I haven't tracked that one down yet. But our container for post merge blocks is definitely out of alignment with the spec. Hoping to track down the other bug today
